newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firmer in early bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares firmer in early bourse dealings.

text.p: German shares were higher in early thin bourse dealings on Friday, helped by overnight gains on Wall Street and firmer German debt prices.
The 30-share DAX index was up 24.70 points at 2,683.95, or up nearly one percent, as the dollar also underpinned shares.
But trading volumes were thin due to a holiday in many regions of Germany.
Dealers said they were unwilling to make dramatic moves ahead of important U.S. data due out in the afternoon after the close of Frankfurt floor dealings.
The banking sector continued to attract attention after the publication of nine-month results on Thursday.
Daimler Benz was the most heavily traded stock in early computer trade one of the biggest DAX gainers, rising 1.90 marks to a new year's high at 90.80 marks.
Talk in the market about the company's restructuring and its new "smart car" were helping the stock, traders said.
Volkswagen was also stronger than the market, rising 14.75 marks to 611 marks due to ongoing buying after brokerage Merrill Lynch named it a Global Focus One stock.
